chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, raising it, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Jafar (peace be upon him), who said:
The sick person indicates with gestures.
ai.seo_question: How should a sick person perform prayer if they cannot stand or bow physically?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *iima'* (gestural indication) for the sick, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on ease (*taysir*) when physical capacity is diminished. It serves as a foundational text for the hierarchy of prayer postures, where the head nod supersedes other gestures when even sitting is difficult, aligning with the Prophetic tradition that 'pray standing, if you cannot, then sitting, and if you cannot, then lying down.'
